title: Double-Checked Locking without Memory Barriers
pattern: Performing an unsynchronized read of a shared pointer/variable, then acquiring a lock, and verifying the variable again before initializing it, using non-atomic mutable accesses.
why_bad: Compilers and CPUs reorder instructions for performance. Without explicit memory barriers, another thread may observe a partially initialized object (e.g., the pointer is allocated, but fields are not populated), causing unpredictable crashes when reading the fields [39:62].
detection: Performing an unsynchronized conditional check on a non-atomic mutable variable before entering a synchronized lock block that writes to the same variable [39:62].
fix: Utilize standard language primitives (like `std::sync::Once` or atomic types with `SeqCst`/`Acquire`/`Release` ordering) that emit the necessary memory fence instructions [39:62].
